q: The Anosov closing lemma states that near a recurrent point of an Anosov diffeomorphism, there is a periodic orbit. More precisely: for any recurrent point x and ε > 0, there is a periodic point y with d(Tⁿy,Tⁿx) < ε for 0 ≤ n ≤ period(y). This follows from the shadowing lemma because:
opts: A recurrent orbit is a pseudo-orbit (it returns near itself), and the shadowing lemma provides a true periodic orbit that shadows it
The Markov partition gives the closing directly
exp: Closing lemma for Anosov maps: a recurrent point gives a pseudo-orbit (the orbit eventually returns near its start), and the hyperbolic shadowing lemma says this pseudo-orbit is shadowed by a true orbit that must be periodic (since it shadows a nearly-periodic sequence). This gives the density of periodic points in Ω(T).
